content: Support group accused of incitement to subversion case, Lee Cheuk-yan and Chow Hang-tung who pleaded not guilty have gone through 24 days of trial, and the verdict is set for August 21 (Friday). Former vice-chairperson of the Support group, Chow Hang-tung, who is a barrister, represented herself in this case. While in prison without a computer or internet access, she wrote hundreds of pages of submissions by hand, one page at a time. At her application, the court played in full two years of June 4th candlelight assemblies, recreating the candlelight in Victoria Park bit by bit, as well as the testimonies of June 4th witnesses. "So I am the last defendant, and also the last vice-chairperson of the first defendant in this case, the Support group... I'm now 41 years old, a barrister, and there isn't much else to my background." Chow Hang-tung said with a laugh at the start. During the six days of testimony, she smiled from time to time, but also shed tears several times. What does the June 4th assembly and ending one-party dictatorship mean to Chow Hang-tung? What is her "intent"? This episode of the podcast continues to bring readers to the courtroom, using voice acting to recreate Chow Hang-tung's testimony and the questioning from the judge and prosecution. Recap: Voice acting – Lee Cheuk-yan's testimony: In my heart there is no hostility, only love Support group case related reports
